legalName: Motion for Expungement for Misdemeanor Conviction for a First Offense Possession of Marijuana (La. C.Cr.P. arts. 977(D), 998)

componentsNotGenerated.conditionTheRecordStates: Generated only where the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) exemption, whose grounds are non-conviction grounds and so rarely reach this track.
componentsNotGenerated.whyNotGenerated: the condition is that the participant may qualify for the Article 983(F) exemption, whose grounds the record itself describes as non-conviction grounds that rarely reach this track. Article 977(D) is a CONVICTION track, so nothing on either fixture establishes the condition and the component is not generated. The record's own words about the exemption, the fifteen-day return and the non-refundable fee are carried in the participant and filing instructions, and item 4 of the record's required-before-filing list, which claims the packet gives the participant this form, is printed unchanged and corrected beneath.

routeSelectionNote: This packet is built for exactly one route: expungement of a misdemeanour conviction for a FIRST OFFENCE possession of marijuana under La. C.Cr.P. art. 977(D), on the Article 998 form Article 986 makes mandatory for the category. The route is stated on the face of the motion in its title, in its Part II heading and in its recital, and again on the proposed Article 992 order, rather than left as a blank election. What is NOT stated by the packet is whether this particular conviction was in fact the mover's first possession offence: the route fixes the article and the form, the mover's own criminal history fixes that answer, so the election is declared determinedByTheCaseNotTheRoute with the reason recorded, left blank, and disclosed in the guide's supply table beside the record's own first self-help stop condition.

routeSelectionsMade.authority: La. C.Cr.P. arts. 977(D) and 998, with the Article 991 and Article 992 statutory orders
routeSelectionsMade.statedOnTheFaceOfThePacket: the motion is titled and recited as a motion for expungement for misdemeanor conviction for a first offense possession of marijuana, its Part II heading is the statutory one, and the proposed Article 992 order carries the same identification of the record

electionsLeftToTheParticipantAndWhy.whyTheRouteCannotDetermineIt: the route determines the ARTICLE and the FORM and not whether this conviction was in fact the mover's first possession offence. That is a fact of the mover's own criminal history, the committed legal-design limitation classifies it as a participant question and calls it the whole eligibility test for this route, and the record makes the opposite answer the first of its self-help stop conditions.

canonicalRefusals.why: the committed memo makes marijuanaFirstOffense a required participant input, the committed legal-design limitation classifies it as a participant question and calls it the whole eligibility test for this route, and the platform holds no value for it. It is a sworn averment about the mover's own criminal history and no packet may supply it; a second or later possession offence falls back to Article 977(A), which the record makes the first of its self-help stop conditions.
canonicalRefusals.whyTheRouteCannotDetermineIt: the route determines the ARTICLE and the FORM - Article 977(D) on the Article 998 form - and not whether this conviction was in fact the mover's first possession offence. That is a fact of the mover's own criminal history established by their record rather than by the route, and the committed limitation classifies it as a participant question. Writing an answer the record does not establish would put an unsupported averment on a motion the mover signs, and the record makes the opposite answer a condition on which self-help stops.
